problem.explanation: CASE maps salary ranges to labels while retaining every row. Because the first true branch wins, the high threshold must come before medium. A common mistake is using > instead of >= at boundaries. A lookup table is an alternative when tiers change frequently.
hints: CASE conditions are checked from top to bottom.
Test the highest threshold first so it is not captured by the medium branch.
problem.reference_solution: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary >= 80000 THEN 'High' WHEN salary >= 50000 THEN 'Medium' ELSE 'Low' END AS bonus_tier FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC
problem.statement_markdown: Classify every employee as High when salary is at least 80000, Medium when at least 50000, otherwise Low. Return name and bonus_tier, highest salary first.
problem.title: Employee bonus classification
